To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
P25–Ti02 nanoparticles, TiO2 nanowires, and nanotube are found to be highly effective against Gram-negative bacterium, Agrobacterium under UV-irradiation.
photoirradiated P-25 TiO2 nanoparticles, rods and tubes have bactericidal effect on A. tumefaciens cells and the effect was found to be more pronounced for the nanoparticles.
the bactericidal activity is in the order: P25-TiO2 > nanorod > nanotube and this is reverse to the specific surface area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the shape-dependent bactericidal effect of photoirradiation of TiO2 in aqueous medium for the first time.
the bactericidal effect of TiO2 nanoparticles, TiO2 nanowires, and TiO 2 nanotubes on Gram-negative bacterium A. tumefaciens.
the shape-dependent photoactivity of TiO2 nanoparticles, and the mechanism of bactericidal action of TiO2 on the cell surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

P25–Ti2O nanoparticles with the highest specific surface area (54 m2 g–1) and the highest photoactivity is not due to its surface area as their shape, surface structure, and surface morphology are different.
the photoinduced bactericidal activity for the killing of Agrobacterium is in the order of nanotube < nanorod (anatas) < nanoparticles (P-25).
the photoinduced bactericidal activity is dependent on the shape of TiO2 particles, and TiO nanorods and nanotubes exhibit less activity than TiO2 nanoparticles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TiO2 thin film is more effective in the killing of bacteria in comparison to its aqueous slurry, and TiO-2 nanoparticles are more active than nanorods and nanotubes.

the bactericidal activity for the killing of A. tumefaciens is in the order of P25–nanoparticle > nanowire > nanosheet, and the bactericidal effect is due to the generation of reactive oxygen species and the loss of membrane permeability.
TiO2 nanoparticles, rods and tubes have different bactericidal activities and the highest bactericidal activity was found to be with the P25–TiOsuspensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the photoactivity of TiO2 nanoparticles for the killing of bacteria depends on their shape and size, and the highest photoactivity was observed for the TiO2 nanoparticles as compared to nanorods and nanotubes.

the photoactivity of TiO2 nanoparticles, rods, and nanotube for the killing of A. tumefaciens is in the order of nanoparticles > nanowires > nanofibers which is not related to their surface area, rather to the surface morphology and crystal structure of the TiO2.
the shape of TiO2 has a significant effect on the antimicrobial activity and the mechanism of killing is different for different shapes of TiO2 nanoparticles.
